market_context.summary: A strong broad tape with the energy complex being sold against it. SPY closed 773.50 (+1.55%) on 2026-09-21 while XLE fell 2.88%, DINO 5.70% and DVN 2.10% — that divergence is a geopolitical risk premium deflating, not a market event. WTI fell a fourth consecutive session to $95.59 (-4.69%) as Trump declined to strike Yemen and signalled openness to Iran diplomacy, with OPEC and the IEA both cutting 2026 demand outlooks. That single move splits the energy book rather than moving it: falling crude is revenue lost for a pure E&P and feedstock saved for a refiner, and product cracks are at all-time records (3-2-1 at $69.66/bbl, diesel above $106/bbl) on 97.2-98% refinery utilisation and distillate inventories 14% below the five-year average. Rates are the other pressure: US10Y at 5.01% sits 113bp above the 3.88% effective fed funds rate, and the Kalshi ladder prices a 25bp HIKE at 53% for October and 67% by December with a cut at essentially zero. Merchant power keeps de-rating (VST -22.9% off high, CEG -31.2%) even as insiders buy it.

entry.condition: Accumulate in thirds at or below 136 — at or under the CEO's own $135.25-135.99 cost. Second third at 132 near the 200-session low of 132.66. Final third only under 126.

INVALIDATION (not a stop): ERCOT 2027 forward power prices staying at the ~$30/MWh year-to-date level into 2027 guidance, or management cutting the reaffirmed $6.8-7.6B FY26 adjusted EBITDA range. Either means the merchant-scarcity thesis is wrong rather than early, and the position is sold regardless of price.

catalyst.event: AI/datacenter load growth in ERCOT and PJM against a merchant fleet the market is pricing at 10.8x EV/EBITDA while EBITDA grows 30% — accumulate the de-rating rather than wait for a print
catalyst.action: Build in thirds over the next two quarters at 136 / 132 / 126. No urgency — the driver is a multi-year supply-demand imbalance, not a dated event. Do not chase above 140.

recommendations.thesis: Vistra is 22.9% below its high on a power-price de-rating while the business compounds: Q2-26 ongoing-ops adjusted EBITDA was $1.767B, up more than 30% year over year, and management reaffirmed FY26 guidance of $6.8-7.6B. That leaves it at roughly 10.8x EV/EBITDA on the $7.2B midpoint for a nuclear-and-gas fleet sitting in ERCOT and PJM, the two grids most exposed to datacenter load, with long-term supply deals already signed with Meta and AWS. The tell is that CEO James Burke bought 8,665 shares for $1.17M in the open market across 08-24, 08-31 and 09-01 at roughly $135, through a vehicle that already held 1.15M shares.
recommendations.key_risk: THE NUMBER THE THESIS TURNS ON WAS NEVER FETCHED. The whole argument is that ERCOT and PJM 2027 forward power prices rise as datacenter load arrives, and no 2027 forward quote appears anywhere in this run — the only power price actually sourced is the ~$30/MWh year-to-date realised level, which is the idea's own stated invalidation condition. The position is therefore long a curve nobody here has priced, and the $7.4-7.8B 2027 EBITDA opportunity that framed the old valuation is the thing at stake; that is the path to the $106 low end of the analyst range. Second, the money is getting expensive: the 09-14 424B2 prices $1.5B of junior subordinated notes at 7.000% and 7.250% to 2057, junior to about $18.3B of existing senior debt, to refinance preferred resetting in October and December 2026. Paying 7%+ against a 5.01% ten-year is a real cost of carrying the fleet, and the Kalshi ladder prices a hiking path at 53% October and 67% December, which makes that cost more likely to rise than fall. Third, added by the red team: this sits alongside the open CEG position, so merchant power is the one driver in this book carried twice — size the pair, not the ticker.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the CEO is talking down the very prices he is buying the stock on — Burke said publicly that ~$30/MWh ERCOT does not support new construction. The idea's answer is that a price too low to build at suppresses new supply into rising datacenter load. RED TEAM: that answer is not falsifiable as written — it makes a low power price bullish (supply discipline) and a high one bullish (earnings), so no observed price can refute it. It is retained as a plausible reading, not as a confirmation, and it is one of the two reasons conviction came down. The second objection, that the September filings signal distress, is answered by reading them: debt refinancing preferred, not equity, so no dilution — but that establishes the absence of a negative rather than the presence of the thesis, which is the other reason. What survives as genuine independent confirmation is three things, not five: the 10.8x EV/EBITDA against reaffirmed $6.8-7.6B FY26 guidance, the fetched technical structure, and a CEO open-market buy — and that buy is 8,665 shares added to a vehicle already holding 1,146,352, a 0.76% increment, which is a gesture rather than a signal. VST-versus-CEG revision divergence (91.7% bullish +0.4 against 82.1% -3.1) and VST +1.32% against XLU -7.11% over one month remain the best evidence that the merchant de-rating is not uniform.

evidence.detail: CEO/President James Burke bought 8,665 shares for $1.17M open-market via JAMEB LP on 2026-08-24 (2,000 @ $135.00), 08-31 (2,200 @ wtd-avg $135.99) and 09-01 (4,465 @ wtd-avg $135.25); the vehicle already held 1,146,352 shares. Finnhub independently confirms the 08-24 tranche as code P. Analyst revision direction improving at 91.7% bullish; VST +1.32% vs XLU -7.11% over one month.

Read the 2026-09-14 424B2: $850M 7.000% Series A and $650M 7.250% Series B junior subordinated notes due 2057, ~$1.48B net proceeds to redeem preferred stock resetting in Oct and Dec 2026, subordinated to ~$18.3B senior debt. Debt refinancing, not an equity raise — no dilution.

10.8x EV/EBITDA on the reaffirmed $7.2B FY26 adjusted EBITDA midpoint. Street median 12-month target $221 across 20 analysts, mean ~$225, range $106-$305. Target 190 is set 14% below the median; the 112 bear case is set near the $106 low end rather than off the chart.

exit.scale_plan: Hold 12-24 months into the DFARS 2027 demand step-up. Trim a third at 74, the street consensus cluster; let the rest run toward the $100 high estimate only if 10X Facility magnet output is actually shipping. INVALIDATION (not a stop): the 2027-01-01 DFARS 252.225-7052 expansion being delayed or waived, or the DoD $110/kg contract-for-difference being renegotiated. Those two are the whole floor; market NdPr staying below $110/kg is expected and is what the floor is for.

catalyst.event: DFARS 252.225-7052 expands 2027-01-01, requiring covered defense procurement NdFeB magnets to be free of covered-country material across mining, refining, separation and finished magnet — a legislated demand floor that does not depend on the 09-23/25 Trump-Xi summit outcome
catalyst.action: Wait for the summit to clear, then accumulate in thirds at 50 / 45 / 40. The near-term binary is diplomacy; the thesis is the 2027 procurement rule and the DoD price floor, and both survive either summit outcome.

recommendations.thesis: MP is the only US integrated rare-earth miner-to-magnet producer and its downside is contracted rather than hoped for: the DoD holds a 10-year price floor at $110/kg on NdPr structured as a contract-for-difference, which already paid $17.6M of real price-protection income in Q2-26, plus a 10-year guarantee that 100% of 10X Facility magnet output is bought. Q2-26 NdPr production was 840 metric tons, up 41% year over year. From 2027-01-01 DFARS 252.225-7052 bars covered-country material from defense NdFeB magnets across the whole chain, which converts a policy preference into a procurement requirement.
recommendations.key_risk: Insider flow is the loudest argument against and it is not answered: over six months MP shows 2 open-market buys by a single buyer for $1.51M against 20 sells for $79.9M, net -$78.4M. The stock also lags everything measured — -10.59% vs SPY over one month, -20.98% over three, and -3.99% vs XLB over one month — so this is buying a laggard, not leadership. And the street is crowded: 18-19 analysts at Strong Buy with a LOW estimate of $61, above the $50 spot, meaning nobody is positioned for disappointment. If a Trump-Xi deal restores Chinese magnet flows and market NdPr stays far below $110/kg, MP collects the floor and earns nothing above it, and the 200-session low of 37.81 does not hold.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that MP is a policy stock whose entire premium evaporates the moment Washington and Beijing agree — and that case is strong enough that entry is refused before the summit rather than argued past. The position this idea takes is narrower: the $110/kg contract-for-difference and the 2027-01-01 DFARS rule are contractual and statutory, they are unaffected by a tariff handshake, and they will still be there on 09-26 at a price the summit has already set. RED TEAM, on why conviction came down to 3: the loudest objection is the one the idea concedes it cannot answer — 20 insider sells against 2 buys, net -$78.4M over six months, with the people closest to the DFARS timetable selling into it. On top of that the street consensus is doing two contradictory jobs at once: it is the valuation_anchor holding up the 74 target and it is simultaneously named in key_risk as a crowding hazard, because 18-19 Strong Buys with a LOW target of $61 above a $50 spot means nobody is positioned for disappointment. And the dated_catalyst is 2027-01-01, fifteen months beyond any window this entry plan operates in — a real date, but not one that pays you for being early. Three evidence kinds are listed and one of them is doing no work in the horizon traded.

data_quality_notes:
RESEARCH RAN TO COMPLETION. notes.md carries a final RESEARCH COMPLETE block (06:31 ET, superseding two earlier ones at 06:33 and 06:38 whose stamps had drifted), so `truncated` is false and nothing here is reconstructed from fragments. All ten candidates were captured in candidates.jsonl during research, first capture at 06:06; this report is an edit of that file, not a reconstruction. Run was 06:01-06:31 ET.

PRICES ARE THE 2026-09-21 CLOSE, NOT LIVE. Every quote was re-fetched at synthesis and returned session `pre` with an age of ~872 minutes — the US equity market is closed pre-open, so the previous close is the freshest honest price, not stale data.

WHY THE MIX LOOKS LIKE THIS: 8 swing, 2 long_term, 0 intraday, and all ten are equities. Nothing was dropped or promoted for balance. No intraday idea cleared the bar because there was no live index, VIX or futures quote to set precise levels from, and inventing them would have been the worse failure. Crypto, futures and event contracts were each screened and each is documented empty with a reason: BTC at 86,059 with no dated catalyst is not an edge; /MCL was rejected specifically because no WTI price could be fetched; and the Kalshi ladder prices October/December hikes at 53%/67%, which agrees with what US2Y at 4.76% already implies, so there is no probability disagreement to trade.

FOUR OF TEN ARE EXITS, AND THAT IS THE DAY'S FINDING. Five of the sixteen open positions carry no stop at all, and the three of those sitting at 52-week lows — NKE, LCII, LULU — are all being closed. A fourth, DVN, sat 0.51 ATR from its stop with its driver broken. None of the four is a short: they are full exits of existing longs, so `exit.target` and `stop` are null by construction and reward-to-risk does not apply to them.

RATIOS CLUSTER JUST ABOVE THE FLOOR, AND IT IS WORTH SAYING SO. The four new swing ideas recompute to 2.10 (DINO), 2.13 (JBHT), 2.24 (CAG) and 2.97 (KMX) against a 2.0 floor, with stops at 2.06, 2.11, 2.09 and 2.01 ATR against a 2.0 ATR floor — three of the four clear by less than 0.11 ATR of slack. That pattern is the signature of levels fitted to the bar, so it is flagged rather than left for the reader to notice. Against that reading: every target here sits on a level that exists on the tape rather than above it — JBHT 272 is both the 273.05 gap origin and the SMA50 at 271.28, CAG 16.60 is under the 16.735 swing high, KMX 64.50 is under the 65.28 range high — and the KMX entry was moved 7% BELOW spot precisely because the idea failed its floor at 57.86 and the stop was not walked in to rescue it. I recomputed all six ratios and all four ATR stop distances from freshly fetched history rather than trusting the numbers in the notes; they agree.

TWO IDEAS SAY DO NOT BUY TODAY. MP (wait) must not be entered before the 09-23/25 Trump-Xi summit resolves, and KMX (wait) must not be entered before the 09-29 print — and its order is cancelled, not filled, if the entry zone is reached only because that print was bad.

CONVICTION: one deliberate under-claim, disclosed. DVN carries three distinct evidence kinds, which supports a 4, and is published at 3. It is an exit, and under-claiming was preferred to inflating. Every other score equals its distinct-kind count exactly.

SOURCES THAT FAILED, AND WHAT IT COST: query1/query2.finance.yahoo.com returned HTTP 429 on every index and history call and 401 on options, finnhub gates index quotes behind a subscription, stooq 404s on ^-prefixed tickers, and there is no AlphaVantage key. Consequence: no SPX/NDX/DJI/RUT level, no VIX, no DXY, no /ES or /NQ, and no spot gold or WTI quote all run — those entries are null in `market_context.levels` rather than estimated, and the crude and rates figures used come from fetched news and FRED and are sourced as such. No options-implied move on any candidate (yahoo-options 401), which matters most for CAG and KMX, both in front of 09-29 prints. No short interest (api.nasdaq.com timeout). CoinGecko failed once and succeeded on retry; nasdaq history for KMX likewise.

CROSS-CUTTING RISK: the Kalshi ladder prices a HIKING path (53% October, 67% December, cut at zero). That confirms the held TLT short and the decision to close rate-sensitive LCII, and it adds risk to KMX (used-vehicle affordability is a financing story), JBHT (cyclical freight) and CAG (a bond-proxy staple).
